entries.appliesTo: addictive social media platforms (algorithmic content selection + addictive features) with child (under 16) account holders resident in North Carolina

dutySources.age-assurance: § 114B-3(a) — 'An addictive social media platform shall use either anonymous age verification or standard age verification to verify that an account holder is 16 years of age or older'
dutySources.takedown-process: § 114B-2(c)(2) — 'Allow the parent or guardian of an account holder who is 14 or 15 years of age to request that the child's account be terminated. Termination must be effective within 10 business days after the request.'

exposure.enforcer: attorney-general (exclusive UDTP action) + private-right (child account holder, damages up to $10,000)

sources.minorsFocus: § 114B-1(b)(4) — 'Child. – A person who is under 16 years of age.'
sources.penaltyMax: § 114B-2(d)(2) — 'the Attorney General may collect a civil penalty of up to fifty thousand dollars ($50,000) per violation and reasonable attorneys' fees and court costs'
sources.enforcer: § 114B-2(d) — 'an unfair and deceptive trade practice under G.S. 75-1.1'; § 114B-2(d)(1) — 'The action may solely be brought by the Attorney General against an addictive social media platform.'; § 114B-2(e) — 'An addictive social media platform that knowingly or recklessly violates this section is liable to the child account holder … Claimants may be awarded up to ten thousand dollars ($10,000) in damages.'

flags: parental-consent requirement for 14-15-year-old account holders (§ 114B-2(c): platform 'shall prohibit a child who is 14 or 15 years of age from entering into a contract … unless the child's parent or guardian provides consent') fits no fixed duty — consent-workflow covers likeness/replica/data use only
mandatory account termination with 30-day dispute window and permanent deletion of personal information (§ 114B-2(b)(1)-(2)) has no fixed duty key

flat prohibition on using a child's user data for algorithmic content recommendations, targeted advertising, or sale to third parties (§ 114B-3.5(a)) is a ban, not an opt-out — stronger than the admOptOut param, so not coded

applicability threshold — 10% or more of daily active users younger than 16 spending on average at least two hours per day (§ 114B-1(b)(2)b.) — not expressible in privacy-data params (userThreshold exists only in provenance-transparency)

age tiers not expressible in privacy-data params: under-14 accounts prohibited outright (§ 114B-2(b)); 14-15 permitted only with parent/guardian consent (§ 114B-2(c)); verification threshold is '16 years of age or older' (§ 114B-3(a))
anonymous age verification must be offered alongside standard verification and the user selects the method (§ 114B-3(a)); anonymous method carries data-minimization requirements (§ 114B-1(b)(3))

enforcement routes through UDTP G.S. 75-1.1 / Chapter 75 with an additional civil penalty under G.S. 75-15.2 — cross-referenced amounts not coded per rule 4; the $50,000 penalty stated in this text is coded
punitive damages available for 'a consistent pattern of knowing or reckless conduct' (§ 114B-2(d)(3))
Part I effective January 1, 2027, applying to causes of action arising on or after that date (Section 1.(b))
text on file is Sixth Edition Engrossed (6/10/26); data/legiscan.js status is 'Engrossed', not chaptered — not final enacted text; no replaced-by relation present

AI nexus is definitional: platform coverage requires 'algorithms that analyze user data or information on users to select content for users' (§ 114B-1(b)(2)c.), and § 114B-3.5(a)(1) bars data 'from being used in an algorithm to generate algorithmic recommendations'

entries.appliesTo: State Board of Education, Department of Public Instruction, and governing bodies of public school units (local boards, charter schools, regional schools, lab schools)

dutySources.risk-program: Section 3.(b), G.S. 115C-47(73) — 'Local boards of education shall adopt a policy on the use of artificial intelligence by students and staff for educational purposes after review of the model policy developed by the Department of Public Instruction pursuant to G.S. 115C-102.13.'

sources.curriculum: Section 2.(a), G.S. 115C-81.90(a1) — 'The State Board shall adopt age-appropriate standards for instruction on artificial intelligence (AI) literacy for grades kindergarten through 12. All courses offered pursuant to this section shall include instruction on AI literacy aligned with the standards adopted by the State Board.'
sources.policyRequired: Section 3.(b), G.S. 115C-47(73) — 'Local boards of education shall adopt a policy on the use of artificial intelligence by students and staff for educational purposes'
sources.trainingRequired: Section 5.(d) — 'All teachers employed by local school administrative units, charter schools, or laboratory schools shall complete the professional development provided pursuant to this section by June 30, 2028.'

flags: Parts II, IV, and V primarily direct state education agencies (State Board of Education, Department of Public Instruction) — e.g. DPI 'shall establish and maintain an evaluation framework' for generative AI educational tools, maintain a 'publicly available list of AI tools that have been reviewed' and 'a publicly available list of all AI tools being used in public school units', and establish 'procurement guidance, qualified vendor lists' (§ 115C-102.14) — no matching education-k12 param

DPI model AI policy must include AI literacy education 'about nonconsensual intimate imagery' (§ 115C-102.13(2)); model policy due December 31, 2026, with unit access by January 15, 2027 (Section 3.(g))
governing bodies must adopt AI use policies by June 30, 2027 (Section 3.(g))
AI literacy standards must be reviewed and updated 'every two years' (§ 115C-81.90(a1)); revised computer science standards implemented beginning with the 2028-2029 school year (Section 2.(b))

training modules 'require a minimum of 10 hours of seat time to complete' (Section 5.(b)(1)); developed with the Friday Institute at NC State; resources available to public school units by June 30, 2027 (Section 5.(c))
DPI reporting to Joint Legislative Education Oversight Committee due December 15, 2028 (Sections 2.(d), 5.(e))
no penalty or enforcement provision in Parts II-V — exposure omitted (rule 3)
